title: HaNDF: Object-Conditioned Geometric Neural Hand Distance Fields
claim: A condition-specific learned manifold of plausible configurations lets noisy poses be projected onto valid ones, supporting generation, completion and real-world recovery.
layout: Left 2 landscape panels with trajectories, right 2x2 application gallery; left-to-right
description: The left two-thirds show two 3D-rendered tabletop scenes. Each has an object (a pink camera labeled z1, an orange bottle labeled z2) beside a wavy wireframe surface labeled S(z1) and S(z2), representing the zero-level set of the object-conditioned field. A chain of blue hands, from a noisy initial pose θ0 to a final pose θT marked by a red dot, follows an orange curve down onto the surface. The hand ends up grasping the object, and the second scene is labeled 'Denoising'. The right third is a gallery of four application results with rotated labels: Generation (multicolored hands around a bottle), Completion (translucent hand and object with dashed circles), and In-the-wild Recovery (a kitchen photo next to a reconstructed jug and hand mesh). The eye goes first to the hand trajectories and the landscape surfaces.
caption: We introduce HaNDF, an object-conditioned generative hand prior. HaNDF is a geometric neural distance field representing the plausible hand configurations under interaction, and enables numerous tasks from denoising and completion to recovering hands or even objects from image data.\vspace{-3mm}
abstract: We propose, HaNDF, object-conditional neural distance fields as data-driven priors for modeling the plausible hand-object configurations, in the product manifold of hand articulations. While recent unconditional generative priors showed success in modeling human pose, hands are versatile articulated bodies often found in interaction with other objects. This makes it crucial to develop a generative prior which can model the plausible hand poses conditioned on the object under interaction. To this end, our HaNDF proposes a geometry-aware, object-conditioned neural distance field, representing the plausible articulations in the zero-level set of a conditional field. We leverage tools from Riemannian geometry to (i) represent plausible hands in the zero level-set of an object-induced neural field, and (ii) project a given pose onto this field. Using HaNDF, we can also optimize for a plausible condition, determining the object under interaction. Our extensive evaluations demonstrate that our HaNDF provides a flexible and powerful prior for hand-object interaction, suitable for applications such as pose refinement, reconstruction under occlusion, and physically plausible manipulation synthesis.
